scope: Actual original detail inspection of sheep-sabbath01-02, including direct canonical Christ pixel comparison for02.
globalConditions: Technical acceptance is not owner approval or browser verification.

entries.alt: A cream-fleeced sheep with a dark face and drooping ears stands at the bottom of a rocky earthen pit and looks upward.
entries.caption: Jesus asks His hearers to consider a sheep that has fallen into a pit on the Sabbath. The vulnerable animal makes His question about practical care immediate and recognizable.
entries.findings: Animal anatomy is coherent with visible legs planted on ground, natural muzzle/ears/eyes and wool texture. No wounds or implausible body joins. High viewpoint clearly establishes pit depth without claiming an actual recorded rescue location.
conditions: Hypothetical comparison taught by Jesus, not a recorded rescue performed by Him.
Unnamed rescuer and sheep, no authenticated breed/biography/location or healing claim.

entries.recommendedTitle: Lifting the sheep from the pit
entries.alt: A dark-haired bearded man braces inside the pit and supports the sheep beneath its chest as its front hooves reach the grassy edge.
entries.caption: In Jesus' comparison, a person takes hold of the sheep and lifts it out. This imagined rescue pictures the ordinary care He uses to challenge resistance to doing good on the Sabbath.
entries.findings: Same cream fleece, dark gray-brown face, long dark ears and light eyes preserve sheep01 continuity. Visible arm and supporting palm cradle chest behind forelegs; second arm is largely occluded around upper body, with no visible contradictory limb. Front legs extend toward rim and rear body remains supported from below; rescuer braced leg/posture plausible. Gaze attends sheep/edge rather than viewer. Compared actual canonical Christ reference: rescuer has denser black beard, stronger angular brow/long prominent nose and fuller tightly curled dark hair; distinct interpretation, not canonical Christ. Natural skin, wool, terrain and cloth retain photographic realism.
conditions: Hypothetical comparison taught by Jesus, not a recorded rescue performed by Him.
Unnamed rescuer and sheep, no authenticated breed/biography/location or healing claim.
